label: Global mirror image and global handedness: a world map σ and a world feature H that it reverses
term: global mirror image (σ) and global handedness (H)
definition: HandednessReversedAt σ H w := H (σ w) ↔ ¬ H w, for a map σ : W → W on the frame's worlds (the global mirror: σ v is v with everything left made right and right made left, all relations among the parts kept) and a world feature H : W → Prop (global handedness: the actual-handed arrangement obtains). The mirror image of w has the opposite handedness. Both σ and H are explicitly identified PRIMITIVE parameters of TruthCore.Modal.MirrorCollapse; nothing in Lean says that σ preserves every qualitative feature. That clause enters only through the premise EssentialTruthsPreservedByMirrorAt (every ESSENCE_5 truth the actual world satisfies, its mirror image satisfies).
note: Stipulated for #2145 lane M (owner question 2026-11-27; docs/notes/simplicity-collapse-555.md, section on the relation-of-reason account and the mirror-world rule). Navigation only, attribution deferred: the Leibniz–Clarke east–west and translation cases (sourced statement 7dd2af35 concerns translation, not reflection) and Kant's incongruent counterparts. No claim is attributed to them. A relationalist about orientation identifies a world with its global mirror image (σ w = w); then HandednessReversedAt fails for every H. Distinct from translation (TruthCore.Space.TranslationBoundary), which preserves orientation, and from a value tie between qualitatively different arrangements, which a qualitative rule can break.

formal_gap.meaning: σ maps each world to its global mirror image; H holds at a world when its arrangement has the actual handedness. A model supplies both; Lean fixes only their types.
examples: A world containing one left hand and nothing else; its mirror image contains one right hand.
The actual world with every chiral molecule and every helicity reversed.
exclusions: A translation or rotation, which preserves handedness.
A world that differs qualitatively from w (a different arrangement of relations), even if equally good.
Handedness relative to a part of the same world (this hand relative to that one), which the mirror preserves.
open_obligations: Whether global handedness is a genuine feature of a world (orientation substantivalism) or nothing (relationalism): the premise HandednessReversedAt is what the relationalist denies.
Whether σ preserves every qualitative feature: entered only for essential truths, through EssentialTruthsPreservedByMirrorAt.
